info.name: iManage Work Universal API v2 — Workspace Sync
info.description:
Requests for the iManage Work Universal API endpoints used by the Azure Function workspace synchronisation job.

**Source of truth:** iManage Work Universal API Documentation for cloudimanage.com, v2.2.26 (updated 2026-08-04), plus the iManage Work REST API Developer Guide 10.2.3.

### How to use this before your tenant exists
1. Import this collection and the matching environment.
2. Create a Postman Mock Server from this collection (right-click the collection > Mock collection).
3. Set the `baseUrl` environment variable to the mock URL Postman gives you.
4. Send every request. The saved examples come back so you can see the exact response shapes.

When iManage provisions your tenant, change `baseUrl` to `https://cloudimanage.com` and fill in the credential variables. Nothing else changes.

### Authentication
Collection-level auth sends `X-Auth-Token: {{authToken}}` on every request except 'Get access token', which is set to No Auth. Run 'Get access token' first; its test script writes `authToken` into the active environment automatically.

exec: // Surface the rate-limit budget on every call. iManage returns these
// headers when the rate_limiting feature flag is on for your tenant.

item.name: 1 · Authentication
item.description:
`POST /auth/oauth2/token` returns the access token that every other call carries in the `X-Auth-Token` header.

iManage supports four grant types: SAML (RFC 7522), Authorization Code with PKCE (RFC 6749/7636), Password (RFC 6749) and Refresh Token (RFC 6749).

**Password grant constraints, quoted from the iManage docs:** "The password grant can only be used for users that are not synchronized with an external IDP, or if the IDP uses the OIDC protocol with Direct Grant support." The account must also have `allow_logon` set to true.

`client_id` is required for all grant types except Refresh Token. `client_secret` is required if the client is a web application. Both are issued by iManage when your application is registered.

request.description:
Body is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, not JSON.

Token lifetime is configured per iManage environment. When it expires, call this again. iManage warns that a token may be invalidated at any time through expiration or revocation, so the Azure Function must handle a 401 by re-authenticating and resubmitting, not by failing the run.

The test script writes `access_token` into the `authToken` environment variable.

exec: console.warn('No access_token in response. Check client_id, client_secret and grant_type.');

request.description:
`GET https://{hostname}/api` is the discovery call. Note the path is `/api`, **not** `/work/api/v2/...`.

Read `data.user.customer_id` for the customer ID used as a path parameter everywhere else. iManage states this value is permanently and uniquely assigned, so the Function only needs to resolve it once at startup rather than on every cycle.

`data.work.libraries[].alias` gives the library IDs you are entitled to.

item.name: Get features (cloud vs on-prem, rate limiting)

request.description:
Two feature flags matter to this integration.

`cloudimanage` — `true` means the tenant is iManage Cloud at cloudimanage.com and you should read the cloudimanage.com schema variant. `false` means imanage.work or on-premises. Some request and response bodies genuinely differ between the two, so read this once at startup rather than assuming.

`rate_limiting` — `true` means the `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset` response headers are populated and your throttling logic can rely on them.

item.name: 2 · Initial synchronisation
item.description:
One-time backfill of every workspace in the library, run before the polling loop starts.

Two options. `GET .../workspaces` is the search endpoint and works with an ordinary account. `POST .../sync/workspaces/crawl` is purpose-built for bulk export, takes a limit of up to 1000, but iManage restricts it to system users of type `WORK_MIGRATION` or `BACKUP_RESTORE_AGENT`. Confirm with the vendor which account type you will be issued before designing around the crawl endpoint.

request.description:
`GET /work/api/v2/customers/{customerId}/libraries/{libraryId}/workspaces`

Returns a page of workspaces with their full metadata profile, including `custom1` through `custom30`, which is where client and matter values live in most iManage deployments.

Paging uses `paging_mode=standard_cursor` with a `cursor` value carried forward from the previous response. This exact form appears in the official iManage sample request. Keep `sort_order=asc` so the walk is stable across pages.

The response envelope is `{ cursor, data: { results: [], facets: {} } }`. Note that the workspaces cursor format (`31653;1`) differs from the change-events cursor format (`2687321`); they are not interchangeable.

item.name: List workspaces — next page (uses saved cursor)

request.description:
Identical to the first page but sends the `cursor` captured by the previous request. Keep sending this until the response stops returning a cursor.

In the Azure Function this is the backfill loop. Persist the cursor between iterations so a mid-backfill failure resumes rather than restarting.

request.description:
`GET .../workspaces/{workspaceId}`

This is the call the polling loop makes after a change event tells it a workspace changed. Change events carry only the object ID and the action, never the new field values, so the current metadata has to be fetched separately.

Workspace IDs use the `LIBRARY!number` form, for example `ACTIVE_US!7601`.

request.description:
`POST .../sync/workspaces/crawl` — part of the Sync Export collection, designed for crawling through all workspaces in a library.

**Access restriction, quoted from the iManage docs:** "Only system users of the type 'Library Migration' (`WORK_MIGRATION`) or 'Backup and Restore' (`BACKUP_RESTORE_AGENT`) can execute this request."

Body accepts `cursor` (string), `limit` (1–1000, default 100) and `workspace_ids` (array, max 50). The higher limit makes this materially faster than the search endpoint for a full backfill, if your service account qualifies.

item.name: 3 · Change events (the polling loop)
item.description:
`GET /work/api/v2/customers/{customerId}/libraries/{libraryId}/change-events`

Returns events describing actions performed on iManage Work objects. This is what the Azure Function polls on a timer.

**Query parameters:** `actions`, `cursor`, `exclude_app_ids`, `item_types`, `limit` (default 100), `root_id`. That is the complete list for v2.2.26.

**Pagination scheme:** explicit overflow with required cursor. iManage describes this as "intended for continuous scrolling of new results. As the cursor is present even when there are no additional records, the client application may use this cursor to periodically poll for the next page." That property is what makes the cursor safe to persist as your position.

**Workspaces are `container` objects.** A new workspace arrives as `item_type: container`, `action_type: insert`. Metadata edits arrive as `profile_update` or `name_value_pair_update`. The event carries the object ID only, so fetch the profile separately to get the new values.

request.description:
Leave `cursor` empty on the very first call and the result set starts from the beginning of the journal. After that, always send the cursor you stored.

The three disabled parameters are the filters worth switching on once you know what you need:

- `item_types=container` narrows to workspaces and folders, dropping document noise.
- `actions=insert,profile_update,name_value_pair_update` narrows to creation and metadata change.
- `exclude_app_ids` drops events your own application generated, which prevents echo loops if the integration ever writes back.

Filtering server-side is cheaper than filtering in the Function and reduces how quickly you burn the rate-limit budget.

response.name: 429 — rate limited

exec: // The cursor is returned even when there are no new events, so it is a
// durable position marker. Persist it (SQL) after the batch is committed,
// never before, or a crash mid-batch loses events.

request.description:
The filtered form the Function should actually run in production.

`item_types` allowed values: `document`, `container`, `type`, `user`, `group`, `worklist`, `checkout_list`, `sync_preference`, `container_item`, `group_member`.

`actions` allowed values: `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `profile_update`, `security_update`, `document_link`, `container_link`, `document_unlink`, `container_unlink`, `name_value_pair_update`, `declared`, `undeclared`, `container_move`, `restored_from_trash`, `purged_from_trash`, `kmtag_update`.

exec: // The cursor is returned even when there are no new events, so it is a
// durable position marker. Persist it (SQL) after the batch is committed,
// never before, or a crash mid-batch loses events.

item.name: 4 · Change event queues (server-side position)
item.description:
iManage can store your read position for you. A queue is a named bookmark holding the last `event_id` your application processed.

Four operations:

- `POST .../change-events/queues` — create
- `GET .../change-events/queues/{queueId}` — read current position
- `PUT .../change-events/queues/{queueId}` — advance the position
- `DELETE .../change-events/queues/{queueId}` — remove

**Open question for the vendor.** `GET /change-events` accepts a `cursor` parameter but has no `queue_id` parameter, so the queue is not automatically applied to the read. The documented change-events example returns `"cursor": "2687321"`, which has the same format as an event `id`, so the two look interchangeable. The documentation never states this outright. Confirm before relying on it.

request.description:
Body fields: `queue_id` (required, the name of the queue), `event_id` (optional — omit it and iManage defaults to the latest change event for the library), `filter_options` (optional).

Omitting `event_id` means the queue starts at 'now' and you will not receive history. Supply an `event_id` if you want to replay from a known point.

Returns `data.event_id`, the latest event ID recorded against this queue, plus `event_date` showing when the queue was last updated.

Useful as a health check: if `event_date` is hours stale, the Function has stopped advancing.

Body fields: `event_id` (required, max 254 characters), `filter_options` (optional).

Call this after a batch is durably committed downstream, not when it is read. Note that `filter_options` is documented on the response as "[Currently not implemented]", so do not design around it.
Removes the queue. Only relevant for teardown or for deliberately forcing a full reconciliation on the next run.
